The http-kit wrapper base-fn: ~run-server~ spins the listener thread and binds the composed Ring handler to a port, recording ~:network~ / ~:process~ effects. Where a request first enters the web layer, so the natural first stop. Note it is a tiny primitive — everything else is composed from small base-fns in ~web/http/fns.edn~.

The CRUD HTTP surface is one namespace, ~web.crud~, spread over seven modules (~crud~, ~-types~, ~-write~, ~-delete~, ~-seq~, ~-parse~, ~-routes~) — every ~/api/entities/*~ route is a fn-def over base-fns like this one. ~write-rej~ is the whole of stage 2 as ONE library boundary: the cycle / MI / override / list-closed chain from the CRUD block, returned as ~{:reason …}~ or nil, so the parse → validate → apply pipeline is visible in the graph.

* 12. hiccup-element
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: web/hiccup-element
:FILE: resources/packages/web/html/impls.clj
:LINE: 26
:MINS: 1.0
:END:

The generic ~[tag attrs children]~ constructor behind the graph-native page runtime. User-composed pages are fn-defs (~:html-page~, components) that emit hiccup through this primitive — including the ~data-action~ attrs that the editor's JavaScript runtime (~resources/packages/app/editor/*.js~) binds on click — alongside the ~hx-*~ attrs whose server-rendered ~/partials/*~ fragments now carry logic that once lived in that JS. Where a user's page becomes a concrete hiccup tree.

* 15. pick-encoding-fn
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: web/pick-encoding-fn
:FILE: resources/packages/web/http/impls.clj
:LINE: 159
:MINS: 1.6
:END:

The outbound finalizer is a graph composition now — ~:process-response~ in web/http/fns.edn stringifies headers, applies the ~Connection: close~ policy, and encodes the body, all as fn-defs over single-call primitives. This RFC 7231 Accept-Encoding negotiation is the one self-contained parse the pipeline keeps in Clojure; the DECISION to encode (thresholds, compressible pattern) lives in the graph. The last stop as the rendered page leaves the web layer back through http-kit.

- source :: [[file:../../../resources/packages/web/http/impls.clj::(defbase pick-encoding-fn][resources/packages/web/http/impls.clj:159]]

The server-side type-picker sweep behind ~/partials/compatible-type-options~. It filters the ~type-name-kinds~ roster to the names that can legally narrow ~expected~ in ONE alias-aware ~subtype?~ pass — replacing the editor's former per-name fan-out of ~50 parallel ~POST /api/types/compatible~ requests per picker open. The graph-first migration's clearest case: a client loop collapses into one server render.

The old ~?fn=<name>~ per-fn full-entry backfill is gone with its only client consumer — the return-type-rule popover is a server partial now, and the layout strip facts read the raw registry directly. How the type-checker's registry reaches the browser as a lean payload.

* 18. sync-fn-defs-branch!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: web/sync-fn-defs-branch!
:FILE: resources/packages/mcp/mcp/impls.clj
:LINE: 30
:MINS: 3.0
:END:

The web layer has a second client: an AI. The optional ~mcp~ package serves ~/mcp~ (JSON-RPC) through the same per-branch router, and this is its only write primitive — sync fn-defs into a branch, then delta-invalidate THAT branch's registry, not the request's own (the AI writes to ~ai/…~ while its POST rides main). The key design point is in the docstring: writes go through the very ~sync-fns-to-storage!~ the package loader uses, so a proposal from an AI meets the same cycle / collision / type constraints as a human's ~fns.edn~.

- source :: [[file:../../../resources/packages/mcp/mcp/impls.clj::(defbase sync-fn-defs-branch!][resources/packages/mcp/mcp/impls.clj:30]]
